claims.text: Greg Short asserts that early-stage entrepreneurs who focus on profitability metrics and delegation to free up their time are over-optimizing prematurely, because those priorities are appropriate only at a much larger business stage. Taking that advice at the start signals the entrepreneur is listening to someone operating a far bigger operation than they currently have.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: before product-market fit or significant scale
claims.mechanism: Optimization of profitability and delegation presupposes systems and volume that do not yet exist; applying that lens early shifts attention away from the unscalable customer-acquisition actions that actually produce the early traction required for scale.
bounded_by: Does not apply once a business has significant revenue and team size where delegation and margin management become genuine constraints

claims.text: Greg Short asserts that every successful entrepreneur started by doing unscalable, high-volume, direct-contact activities rather than building efficient systems from day one; specifically, spending extra hours in direct one-to-one customer DMs is the correct early-stage strategy.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.mechanism: Direct unscalable contact builds early customer relationships, surfaces product-market feedback, and drives initial revenue without the overhead of systems that would be premature and wasteful before volume is proven.
bounded_by: Not applicable once the business has enough volume that unscalable personal contact becomes a bottleneck rather than an advantage

examples.text: Greg Short describes attaching a Bluetooth keyboard to his iPhone because his thumbs would get sore from the volume of customer DMs he was sending personally. This illustrates that early-stage founder hustle meant doing direct, high-frequency, unscalable customer contact rather than building automation or delegation systems.

practices.text: In the early stage of a business, spend extra hours DMing customers directly rather than building optimization systems or delegation structures.
